The first few days show significant deviations, with true outcomes often differing from predictions. Specifically, the model struggles with accurate initial price forecasting, requiring careful recalibration.

Analyzing the deviations reveals systematic patterns. When sentiment is positive (0.67-1.00), prices tend to be 0.1-0.3 higher than predicted. Negative sentiment (0.00-0.33) correlates with prices being 0.1-0.3 lower. The mean reversion effect becomes evident as prices gradually moving toward the historical average of 76.50.

Key observations emerge: the model consistently underestimates prices during positive sentiment and overestimates when sentiment turns negative. Prices naturally drift back to their mean, correcting extreme movements.
